prompts.title: This week's bake list
prompts.summary: The bake list post, the story frames and the cutoff, from what you plan to bake.
prompts.prompt: This week [bakery] is baking: [items with prices]. Orders close [day/time], pickup is [day, time, place]. Write the bake list post (short, items and prices in a list), three story frames (the list, a close-up, last call), and a pinned comment with how to order: [link].
prompts.use: Post Monday. Repost the last-call frame the night before cutoff.

prompts.title: Saved replies for order DMs
prompts.summary: Answers to the six questions home bakers get every day, in your voice.
prompts.prompt: Write saved replies for [bakery] for: price list, allergens (we bake with [ ]; we can't promise allergen-free), pickup times and place, custom cake requests (what I need to quote), delivery (yes/no and cost), and "are you sold out?". Each under 50 words, friendly, ending with the order link [link].
prompts.use: Save them in Instagram's saved replies or your phone's text shortcuts.

prompts.title: Holiday preorder plan
prompts.summary: A preorder plan for one holiday: the menu, the cutoff, the posts and the pickup slots.
prompts.prompt: Plan [holiday] preorders for [bakery]. I can bake [max] orders. Menu ideas: [ ]. Give: a 4-item holiday menu with prices, the cutoff date, pickup slots, three posts (announce, half sold, last call) and a pickup reminder text.
prompts.use: Start three weeks out. Close orders at your max, not after.

hooks: Home bakers: stop taking orders in DMs.
What a custom cake actually costs you, counting your hours.
The six saved replies every home baker needs.
Close preorders at your max. Here's the post.
Your bake list is your homepage.
Pickup day text that brings people back next week.

legal: Cottage food rules differ by state (what you can sell, labels, where). The pack tells bakers to check their state's rules; copy never says home baking is allowed everywhere.
